deep.reconstruction:
The page is extremely faint. Only fragments can be read with any confidence: the item number '2.', the letters a, b, c(, d), words that look like 'Summen jedes Paares', 'Beispiel', 'Die Bedeutung jeder ...' and 'durch die Formel', and three or four fraction-type formulas in the lower half whose contents cannot be read. Everything below is an interpretation. It is guided by the context: the next page opens a list headed 'Lehrsätze und Aufgaben die complexen Zahlen betreffend', where items 1 and 2 concern 'cyklische Zahlen' (unit-modulus complex numbers), circles, and 'Klise'. This sheet appears to be the reverse of that list and to continue it.

Probable content (interpretive):

(i) Definition (lines 1-5). Four complex numbers a, b, c, d are called harmonically placed (two pairs (a,b), (c,d)) when the product of the sums of each pair equals twice the sum of the products of each pair:
(a+b)(c+d) = 2(ab+cd).

(ii) Equivalence (my filling-in). Expanding gives
(a-c)(b-d) + (a-d)(b-c) = 2ab + 2cd - (a+b)(c+d).
So the condition is equivalent to the cross ratio (a,b;c,d) = (a-c)(b-d)/((a-d)(b-c)) = -1. The four points then lie on a circle, and (c,d) separate (a,b) harmonically. This is presumably the geometric meaning stated in lines 6-8 ('such numbers ... on a circle').

(iii) Example. Probably a simple quadruple; for instance 1, -1, i, -i satisfies the condition.

(iv) General solution (lines 9-10, 'Allgemeine Auflösung'). Given a, b, c, solving the linear equation for d gives
d = (2ab - c(a+b)) / (a+b-2c).

(v) Lines 11-12 onward, 'Die Bedeutung jeder ... durch die Formel', followed by fractions. These are most likely an expression of each number, or of the meaning of the relation, by a fraction-linear (cross-ratio-type) formula, possibly via a parameter x. Possible forms are d - c = ... or x = (a-c)(b-d)/((a-d)(b-c)). Their contents are illegible and cannot be reconstructed with certainty.

(vi) Final lines. A closing remark; legible fragments are too few to restate it.

results.what: Condition for four complex numbers to form a harmonic quadruple: (a+b)(c+d)=2(ab+cd), equivalent to cross ratio -1, meaning concyclic points in harmonic separation (interpretive reading)
results.modern_name: Harmonic quadruple / cross ratio -1 of complex numbers; harmonic conjugate on a circle
results.usually_credited_to: Harmonic division is classical (Apollonius, Desargues, La Hire). Its complex-number / circle-geometry treatment is usually associated with Möbius (Kreisverwandtschaft, 1853-55) and later von Staudt and Klein.

deep.surprise_reason: The page appears to belong to Gauss's list of theorems on the geometry of complex numbers (circles, unit-modulus 'cyclic' numbers). His use of complex numbers in plane geometry is well documented. A harmonic-quadruple criterion would be a minor unpublished detail anticipating Möbius-style circle geometry, but it is elementary. The reading is highly uncertain.
